title: CAD/CAM Theories and Practices
description:
This course aims to develop students’ integrated capabilities in computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/CAM) through English-medium instruction, project-based learning (PBL), case analysis, technical discussion, hands-on practice, and research-oriented training. No prior advanced CAD/CAM or research experience is required. The course is scaffolded from fundamental modeling and manufacturing concepts toward parametric design, mechanism analysis, CAM planning, prototype development, experimental validation, and research communication.
Students will learn to analyze world-class engineering and product design cases, identify their underlying engineering principles, limitations, and innovation opportunities, and transform these observations into researchable engineering questions. The course also introduces literature search strategies, journal quality assessment, research gap identification, and evidence-based technical discussion.
The course does not require a specific CAD/CAM software platform. Selected tools will be demonstrated in class, while students may adopt appropriate software according to project needs. By the end of the course, students are expected to complete a research-oriented PBL project integrating design, analysis, manufacturing, validation, and technical presentation. High-quality projects may be further developed toward journal publication.
Week 1 — Course Introduction: From Zero to Research-Ready
Week 2 — Global Design Benchmarking and Engineering Observation
Week 3 — Literature Search, Journal Selection, and Research Landscape
Week 4 — From Design Case to Research Question
Week 5 — Parametric CAD and Design Variables
Week 6 — Advanced Modeling, Assembly, and Mechanism Design
Week 7 — Simulation, Research Methodology, and Validation Strategy
Week 8 — Research Proposal and Design Review I
Week 9 — Design Optimization and DFMA
Week 10 — CAM Fundamentals and Process Planning
Week 11 — Toolpath Generation and Manufacturing Simulation
Week 12 — Prototype Manufacturing and Assembly
Week 13 — Measurement, Metrology, and Experimental Data Collection
Week 14 — Data Analysis and Digital–Physical Validation
Week 15 — Research Discussion, Contribution, and Paper-Oriented Reporting
Week 16 — Final Research Defense and Prototype Demonstration

title: Servo Control
description:
This course aims to guide graduate students in a deep dive into the control technologies of advanced power converters and electric motor drives, laying a solid foundation for their master's thesis research. The course uses Jose Rodriguez's classic work, *Predictive Control of Power Converters and Electrical Drives* (Wiley, 2012), as the core textbook, and incorporates international journal articles to guide students across theoretical foundations and connect them with cutting-edge international research.
This course fully adopts the flipped classroom model, cultivating students' independent reading, logical reasoning, and academic presentation skills. Students are required to give weekly presentations on key technologies in electric motor servo control, with a particular focus on the theoretical innovation and practical applications of predictive current control. Discussion topics cover finite-state model predictive control, cost function design, simulation, and multi-stage converter integration. The ultimate goal of this course is to help students identify and establish their master's thesis research direction. Through weekly analysis of cutting-edge papers and peer discussions, students can accurately grasp the technological bottlenecks in academia and industry, develop the ability to appreciate international journal articles, possess strong academic expression skills, and cultivate innovative thinking abilities, thereby enabling them to develop forward-looking research.
W1: Introduction
W2-W16: Reports + Lectures on International Journal Articles
Midterm Exam Week: Reports
Final Exam Week: Reports

title: Intelligent Control Systems
description:
This course introduces intelligent control systems, from algorithms to mechanisms, through theory, practical implementation, and publication. Students study systems that perceive, learn, make inferences, and optimize their behavior using incomplete information and under uncertainty.
Theory focuses on three principles of soft computing and artificial intelligence: inference through fuzzy logic for decision-making, learning through neural networks for modeling and error reduction, and evolution through genetic algorithms for optimization and adaptation.
Practical work combines simulation with implementation on aerial, ground, surface, and underwater mobile robots. Problem-based Learning (PbBL) and Project-based Learning (PjBL) develop teamwork through in-class tasks, a concept-generation proposal, and a proof-of-concept project. Publication training develops English academic writing using IEEE paper style.

title: Spectrometer Optical System – Design Principles and Applications
description:
本課程旨在深入探討光譜儀的工作原理與其光學設計的基本理論，並延伸到光譜學分析在產業中的實際應用，讓學生能全面理解光譜儀從物理基礎理論到實際應用的完整過程。除此之外還有實作部分，讓學生有機會參與光譜檢測系統的設計、組裝、控制等應用開發。透過實踐活動，鞏固理論知識、提高實際問題解決能力。
本課程將帶領學生深入了解光譜儀的原理及應用，首先從光譜學的基本概念開始，探討原子光譜成因以及光柵繞射分光的基礎理論，建立學生在光學領域的知識基礎。隨後，課程將轉入光學設計原理，包括聚焦系統與光路設計關鍵要素，使學生能夠理解並設計出有效的光譜儀光學系統。在介紹光譜儀應用部分，將探討UV光譜儀、VIS-NIR光譜儀以及NIR光譜儀等不同型態的操作原理與實際案例，並深入光譜儀在生化檢驗或工業4.0監控場域中的關鍵應用。此外，課程將重點介紹如何利用微型控制器（如Python編程環境下的Raspberry Pi）進行系統整合，培養學生在實際情境中解決問題的能力。最終，在實作環節，學生將進行如水質檢測與顏色辨識等專題項目，這不僅將理論與實踐相結合，也將進一步鞏固學生的專業技能，為日後在科研或產業界的發展奠定基礎。

title: Calculus (I)
description:
微積分是現代科學、工程及人工智慧等領域的重要數學基礎，廣泛應用於各種科學與工程問題。本課程為期一年，將介紹微積分的基本概念與方法，包括極限、微分、積分及偏微分等內容。透過理論講解與實際應用，培養學生理解與運用微積分的基本能力，為未來進階課程及專業領域的學習奠定良好的數學基礎。
Calculus is a fundamental mathematical foundation for modern science, engineering, artificial intelligence, and many other disciplines. It provides essential tools for analyzing and solving a wide range of scientific and engineering problems. This one-year course introduces the fundamental concepts and methods of calculus, including limits, differentiation, integration, and partial differentiation. Through theoretical instruction and practical applications, students will develop essential skills in understanding and applying calculus, providing a solid mathematical foundation for advanced coursework and professional studies.
In this course, I will introduce recent applications of calculus in advanced AI research. Rather than introducing mathematical concepts only from a theoretical perspective, I will first present practical applications to help students understand why these mathematical methods are important and how they are used in real-world AI research.
We will then explore the corresponding concepts and methods in the textbook, followed by a return to the original AI applications. This application–theory–application approach is designed to help students connect mathematical concepts with their practical use and develop a deeper understanding of the subject.
In the TA sessions, we will focus on hands-on calculations and problem-solving. TAs will provide step-by-step explanations of selected textbook exercises and guide students through the calculation process. Through repeated practice, students will become familiar with fundamental calculation techniques and develop the computational skills necessary to apply calculus confidently to problems within each topic.
Topics
1. Functions (Chapter 1)
2. Limits and Continuity (Chapter 2)
3. Derivatives (Chapter 3)
4. Applications of Derivatives (Chapter 4)
5. Integrals (Chapter 5)
6. Applications of Definite Integrals (Chapter 6)
7. Inverse Functions (Chapter 7)

title: Embedded System Design
description:
This hands-on course introduces students to embedded systems, IoT, TinyML, Edge AI, and AI-powered applications through practical, project-based learning. Students will work with the Wio Terminal(Arduino), sensors, actuators, and cloud services to build interactive embedded systems and connected IoT applications.
The course progressively introduces machine learning on embedded devices, including TinyML and Edge Impulse for sensor-based gesture recognition, object detection, sound and motion classification, and anomaly detection. Students will also explore IoT development with Blynk, computer vision with MediaPipe, and AI-assisted application development using NVIDIA DLI and large language models.
Rather than focusing only on individual programming exercises, the course emphasizes integrating hardware, software, data, and AI into functional prototypes. Students will work in small teams to develop their own projects, collect and process real-world data, train and deploy AI models, and demonstrate the resulting systems through a midterm prototype and a final project.
By the end of the course, students will have practical experience designing and implementing AI-enabled embedded systems, from sensor data acquisition and embedded programming to machine learning inference, IoT connectivity, and interactive AI applications.

title: Computer Graphics
description:
電腦動畫、渲染、以及電腦遊戲已經在視聽娛樂以及教育方面扮演了重要的角色。電腦圖學是以上這些進階技術的基本學科。在本課程之中，我們會介紹如何利用電腦來產生以及修改圖形，主要使用的電腦語言為C以及C++。會著重在二維的圖形以及以及三維的圖學上。從這些基本的技進而延伸到進階的電腦圖學、動畫、以及一些電腦遊戲相關的技術。這門課也是之後進階課程的先修課程，包含了電腦動畫、電腦渲染、以及電腦遊戲課程。
"Computer animation, computer rendering, and computer game have become very important in entertainment and education. Computer graphics is the foundation for all these advanced topics. In this class, we would like to introduce the fundamental concepts of using computers to produce and manipulate images using C and C++. Broadly speaking, it will focus on two-dimensional image manipulation and three-dimensional computer graphics (modeling scenes in 3D and producing images of them). Through the process we will introduce the fundamental concepts about computer graphics, computer animation, computer rendering, and the technology of the game programming. This class will become
the prerequisite class for computer animation, computer rendering, and the technology of game programming in the future."

title: Advanced Modern Networking
description:
Recent advances in virtualization technologies are revolutionizing the IT and telecommunications landscapes accelerating their convergence. This course will cover the evolution of computing and networking platforms, with emphasis on the requirements of a service provider. Specific attention will be devoted to Data Center architectures and the concept of virtualization (processing, storage, networking aspects). The course will then address the latest advances and research challenges in Software Defined Networking and Network Function Virtualization concepts and their impact on the design, deployment, and management of ICT services. The course will also address various distributed cloud architectures such as edge and fog computing and research challenges.
1、數據中心網路介紹； 2. 虛擬化網路； 3、虛擬數據中心：存儲、網絡、應用； 4. SDN - 軟件定義網絡、專有和標準解決方案； 5. NFV - 網絡功能虛擬化、提供商網絡中的虛擬化、ETSI 架構、虛擬網絡功能 (VNF) 概念、編排； 6、網絡切片； 7. 5G-MEC：Cloud / Edge / Fog Computing、服務鏈路由、多租戶、多RAT卸載、車載霧； 8. 現有研究問題和未來研究方向。

title: Cybersecurity Threat Analysis and Secure AI
description:
本課程將介紹惡意威脅分析，並以此來探討AI Security(人工智慧安全)領域的兩個面向: “AI for Cybersecurity” (如何利用AI系統來解決資安問題)，以及“Cybersecurity for AI” (AI系統自身存在的資安漏洞)。前者包括AI技術如何應用於惡意威脅偵測等資安議題；後者包括AI系統本身存在的資料隱私安全問題、對抗式攻擊問題、分散式AI計算環境的資安問題等等。最後將結合以上兩者說明如何建構具有安全人工智慧的惡意威脅分析系統。
This course will introduce threat analysis and use it to explore two aspects of AI Security: "AI for Cybersecurity" (how AI systems can be used to address cybersecurity issues), and "Cybersecurity for AI" (the security vulnerabilities inherent in AI systems themselves). The former includes how AI technology can be applied to cybersecurity issues such as malicious threat detection; the latter covers issues such as data privacy security in AI systems, adversarial attacks, and cybersecurity in distributed AI computing environments. Finally, we will integrate the above two aspects to explain how to construct a threat analysis system with secure AI.
一、人工智慧應用於資訊安全
1. 惡意病毒分析簡介
2. 網路威脅分析簡介
3. 靜態分析與動態分析
4. 使用人工智慧進行惡意威脅分析的架構
5. 基於圖像特徵的分析方法
6. 基於自然語言特徵的分析方法
二、資訊安全應用於人工智慧
1. 人工智慧系統的演算法安全問題: 對抗式攻擊
2. 人工智慧系統的資料隱私安全問題: 差分隱私, 同態加密
3. 分散式人工智慧系統的資安問題: 聯邦式學習, 安全多方運算
4. 大語言模型的資安問題
三、兩者整合
1. 基於人工智慧的惡意威脅分析系統面臨的資安議題
2. 邁向具有安全人工智慧的惡意威脅分析系統

title: Engineering Mathematics (1)
description:
Differential equations, which can be classified as either ordinary or partial,  are important/essential for solving many scientific/engineering problems wherein dynamic changes (with respect to time, or position, etc.) are involved. title: Calculus (II)
description:
Calculus is a fundamental course for engineering students. It plays an important role in the understanding of science, engineering, economics, and computer science. Calculus (II) will cover the following topics. The first topic is about how to model the motion of an object by the parametric equations of its position together with how to calculate the derivative and arc length of the corresponding plane curve. Subsequently, the parametric equations of position are transformed into the form of vector-valued function of position such that the velocity and the acceleration can be easily represented by the first and the second derivative in vector form. Second, we will extend the concept of differentiation (i.e., slope) to multi-variable function with respect to each independent variable. This is referred to as the partial derivative, which corresponds to the gradient vector. Gradient vector can be further applied to iteratively optimize the function and has been extensively used for model training in deep-learning applications. The integration of multi-variable function can also be used to estimate the volume under a 2D surface and the moment of mass for a 3D object. Third, the concept of vector field will be introduced. Then, the work done by the vector field on a moving object can be estimated using line integral. Similarly, it is also possible to calculate the flux through a surface or a contour by flux integral in the vector field.
CH 8   Parametric equations and Polar coordinate (參數方程式與極座標)
CH 9   Vectors and Geometry of space (空間向量與空間座標)
CH 10  Vector-valued functions (空間向量函數)
CH 11  Functions of several variables (多變數函數與其導數)
CH 12  Multiple integral (多重積分)
CH 13  Vector analysis (向量分析: 線積分與面積分)

title: Vector Analysis and Complex Variables
description:
The course objectives for Vector Analysis and Complex Variables are as follows:
Vector Analysis
The Vector Analysis course aims to help students understand and apply vector concepts in multivariable calculus. This course primarily covers fundamental theories such as vector fields, line integrals, surface integrals, gradients, divergences, and curls. Through examples, students will deepen their understanding of vector operations in physical phenomena. Ultimately, students should be able to apply these mathematical tools to the field of electrical engineering.
Complex Variables
The Complex Variables course is designed to guide students in gaining a deep understanding of complex number theory and its applications in analysis. The course covers essential concepts such as the basic properties of complex numbers, analytic functions, Cauchy's theorem, and the residue theorem, and applies these theories to problems in physics and engineering. By the end of the course, students should be proficient in the techniques of complex analysis and be able to apply them to solve various complex number-related problems.
This course provides students with a powerful set of mathematical tools, enabling them to gain a deeper understanding and analysis of various phenomena in nature.
The main course content is outlined as follows.
1. Vector functions, gradient field and directional derivatives
2. Divergence and Curl
3. Line integral
4. Surface integral
5. Complex numbers and Complex functions
6. Integration in the complex plane
7. Complex sequences and Series - Taylor and Laurent expansions
8. Singularities and the Residue theorem

title: Probability
description:
This course begins by introducing probability models and their applications in the fields of electrical engineering and computer science. Next, we will cover the fundamental concepts of probability, including probability axioms, counting methods, conditional probability, independent events, and sequential experiments. We will then introduce the concept of random variables, exploring cumulative distribution functions (CDFs), probability density functions (PDFs), functions of random variables, expected values, Markov’s inequality, and various transforms. Subsequently, the course will extend the discussion of a single random variable to multiple random variables. Finally, we will investigate the properties of the sum of multiple random variables, introducing the sample mean, the Law of Large Numbers, and the Central Limit Theorem.
1. Probability Models
2. Probability Axioms
3. Counting Methods
4. Conditional Probability
5. Independence
6. Random Variables
7. Mean and Variance
8. Functions of Random Variable
9. Transform Methods
10. Sums of Random Variables
11. Central Limit Theorem

title: Nonlinear Programming
description:
Optimization is central to any problem involving decision making, whether in engineering or in economics. The task of decision making entails choosing between various alternatives. This choice is governed by our desire to make the “best” decision. The measure of goodness of the alternatives is described by an objective function or performance index. Optimization theory and methods deal with selecting the best alternative in the sense of the given objective function. The purpose of this course is to provide a working knowledge of optimization theory and methods. To accomplish this goal, we include many examples that illustrate the theory and algorithms discussed in the class. However, it is not my intention to provide a cookbook of the most recent numerical techniques for optimization; rather, my goal is to equip the students with sufficient background for further study of advanced topics in optimization.
最佳化是在很多領域中常面對的問題，在決策過程中當面對不同可選擇的可能中，如何選擇最好的是最佳化所要解決的。在這門課中，我們將介紹相關的最佳化理論及方法。基本上，去提供所有的常用可能的最佳化數值技術是不可能，因此，本課程主要在於提供學生充分之知識與概念，以足於當面對任何最佳化問題時知道如何解決。

title: Machine Learning Techniques and Applications
description:
This course equips senior undergraduate and graduate students with fundamental machine learning knowledge and practical model-investigation skills using guided learning activities. Topics include classification, regression, clustering, dimensionality reduction, feature extraction, model evaluation, and introductory deep learning and reinforcement learning. Students are expected to explain modeling choices, interpret validation evidence, identify limitations, compare alternative approaches, and defend conclusions. As an EMI course, students will develop the ability to communicate technical ideas and experimental evidence in English through team investigations, peer questioning, Padlet-based evidence sharing, and oral defense. The four core competencies are Explain, Defend, Critique, and Reflect.
The course begins with the machine learning workflow, including data, features, labels, training, validation, testing, and model evaluation. Students then study major classification methods, including kNN, Naïve Bayes, discriminant analysis, decision trees, SVMs, ensemble methods, and neural networks. Regression topics include linear, robust and regularized regression, support vector regression, regression trees, ensembles, Gaussian processes, and neural networks. The course further covers clustering methods, dimensionality reduction, feature selection, and feature extraction from raw and time-varying signals. Deep learning is introduced through neural representations, transfer learning, training curves, and model limitations. The semester concludes with an evidence-based team symposium and an industry expert workshop on reinforcement learning, while class activities emphasize controlled comparison, evidence interpretation, peer questioning, and English technical communication.

title: Multimedia Communications
description:
This course introduces source coding in information theory and its applications to image and video compression. Topics include visual signal characteristics, image/video formats, entropy coding, Huffman coding, arithmetic coding, and CABAC.
For image coding, classical standards such as JBIG, JPEG, and JPEG 2000 will be covered, including prediction, transform coding, quantization, entropy coding, and rate-distortion optimization. Recent developments in deep image compression and JPEG-AI will also be introduced.
For video coding, the course covers H.261, H.263, MPEG-1/2/4, H.264/AVC, H.265/HEVC, and H.266/VVC. Key technologies such as motion estimation, motion compensation, transform coding, in-loop filtering, rate control, scalability, and CABAC will be discussed.
The course also introduces deep video coding, including learned motion estimation, neural motion compensation, end-to-end rate-distortion optimization, and comparisons with traditional hybrid codecs.
Through lectures, standard documents, software demonstrations, and programming assignments, students will gain a theoretical and practical understanding of modern image and video compression technologies.

description:
The students will learn the knowledge and computational techniques of Linear Algebra, which are indispensable for engineers. Such relation between those two aspects and how they enhance each other will be emphasized in this course.

title: Operating Systems
description:
This course introduces the fundamental concepts and design principles of modern operating systems for students in Information and Communication Technology disciplines. Topics include process management, process synchronization, memory management, storage management, file systems, and system protection and security. Students learn how operating systems manage hardware and software resources, support concurrent execution, and provide secure and efficient computing environments. The course also introduces virtualization technologies, container-based systems, and distributed computing frameworks, forming a foundation for cloud computing and distributed systems.
單元1: 導論: 電腦系統組織、架構與運作方式、資源管理、作業系統服務、系統呼叫、系統結構、建置與開機流程、除錯方法
單元2: 行程管理: 行程概念、排程、行程間通訊（IPC）、多核心程式設計、執行緒模型、排程演算法（FCFS、SJF、RR、優先權）、多處理器排程
單元3: 行程同步: 臨界區問題、硬體支援、互斥鎖（Mutex）、號誌（Semaphore）、監視器（Monitor）、經典同步問題、死結（特性、預防、避免、偵測與回復）
單元4: 記憶體管理: 連續配置、分頁（Paging）、頁表、交換（Swapping）、虛擬記憶體、需求分頁、頁面置換、框架分配、顛簸（Thrashing）
單元5: 儲存管理: 大容量儲存架構、磁碟排程（FCFS、SSTF、SCAN、C-SCAN）、儲存管理、RAID架構、I/O硬體與子系統
單元6: 檔案系統: 檔案概念、存取方法、目錄結構、檔案保護、檔案系統架構、配置方法、空間管理、效能最佳化、回復機制、VFS、NFS
單元7: 保護與安全: 安全問題、程式與網路威脅、密碼學基礎、使用者認證、保護目標、存取矩陣、能力式系統
單元8: 進階主題: 虛擬機器（類型與實作）、分散式系統（網路架構、通訊機制）、分散式檔案系統命名與遠端存取
